newsitem.title: UK: Howard, Lilley quit UK Tory leadership fight.
newsitem.headline: Howard, Lilley quit UK Tory leadership fight.

text.p: Former home secretary Michael Howard and Peter Lilley quit the race for the Conservative party leadership on Tuesday and threw their support behind William Hague, aides for the two men told Britain's PA News Agency.
Lilley came fourth in Tuesday's first ballot, which was won by former finance minister Kenneth Clarke, and Howard came fifth out of a total of five candidates. Hague was in second place.

The news, confirmed to Reuters by an aide to Lilley, was a blow to third placed contender John Redwood. He took 27 votes and then appealed to Howard and Lilley -- both on the right of the party -- to swing their support behind him.

Redwood, who quit the cabinet in June 1995 to mount an unsuccessful challenge to the leadership of the then prime minister John Major, now faces a tough fight to remain in the running for the second round ballot on Tuesday June 17.

The winning candidate needs the backing of more than half of the 164 Conservative MPs remaining after Labour's May 1 election victory. If no one gets the 83 votes required on June 17, the two top candidates go into a final round two days later.
